public_rationale: The prediction concerns GPU demand after OpenAI collapses. The dated service record documents ongoing OpenAI operations, and the search did not establish the required collapse by the cutoff. The antecedent is not met, so NVIDIA's predicted post-collapse sales cannot be scored. Its earlier sales would not resolve this conditional forecast.
limitations: A service-status notice establishes operational activity, not financial health.

The forecast supplies no comparison window or product scope.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: After OpenAI dies, NVIDIA will not be able to justify selling as many GPUs.

statement.excerpt: NVIDIA just won’t be able to justify selling as many GPUs, as it has repeatedly cited OpenAI (albeit without saying its name) as a proxy driver of sales via counterparties including Microsoft and Amazon.

from_speaker: NVIDIA just won’t be able to justify selling as many GPUs
our_interpretation: The collapse condition carries forward from the surrounding passage and means OpenAI ends operations as an AI lab and model provider through business failure.
The ordinary reading is that losing OpenAI-related demand would leave insufficient demand to sustain NVIDIA's pre-collapse GPU sales volume.
As many refers to GPU units, not dollar revenue. The comparison would require comparable periods immediately before and after collapse, adjusted for seasonality and product changes.
The statement about NVIDIA's earlier references supplies the speaker's explanation; it is not separately graded as a historical claim in this forecast assessment.
No deadline or minimum decline is supplied.
criteria.support_condition: After OpenAI collapses, comparable GPU orders or unit shipments show that demand no longer sustains the previous sales volume, with evidence tying the shortfall to lost OpenAI-related demand.
criteria.contradiction_condition: After OpenAI collapses, sustained comparable orders and unit shipments show demand supporting at least the previous GPU sales volume despite the loss of OpenAI-related demand.
